final_answer: Imagine two towns with similar populations and lifestyles. In one town, there are more firefighters responding to fires, and in the other town, fewer firefighters are present. If you observe that the town with more firefighters has more damaged buildings, you might incorrectly assume that firefighters cause more damage. But in reality, the more firefighters are there because the fires are bigger, not the other way around. This illustrates the difference between correlation and causation.
